title: Ajax and asynchronous loading: why the test "flickers"

videos.script: A test that passes on Monday and fails on Tuesday, with nobody touching the code, is usually racing the page. {{flicker}} This lesson is about that race. {{home}} A modern page arrives in two parts. First the document, then the data, which a script asks for afterwards. A test can look in the gap between them and find nothing. {{search}} Then the shop gets a search page. It sends one request for every key you press. Type papaya, and six questions leave at once. {{race}} The short ones take longest, so the answers come back in reverse. And the page shows whichever answer arrived last. {{naive}} You write the obvious tests, and watch them fail, or pass by luck. {{wait}} Then you wait for a state the page announces, instead of a number of seconds. {{defect}} And the honest test fails, every time. The flicker is not in the test. It is a defect in the shop. You report it, and you keep the test watching it until it is fixed. {{end}}
